correctness.rationale: For arbitrary vertex data absolute-value reduction preserves maximal values and decreases variation. The exact three-ball formulas and case split at opposite-part means yield a one-Lipschitz common truncation plus controlled nonnegative error. Summing edgewise and applying Jensen yields the universal upper bound. The point mass attains the stated lower bound, exact subtraction gives a gap below 2/(a+1), and squeezing proves the full uniform joint asymptotic. Finite rational checker independently confirms intermediate inequalities and examples; no infinite conclusion depends on enumeration.

value.rationale: The family consists of dense diameter-two regular/biregular graphs, important for graph BV regularity. The proved uniform sharp asymptotic reveals a genuine balance-dependent phase diagram from 3/2 to 2 even though graph size tends to infinity, contrasting general-graph unboundedness and small-graph contraction results. K_{4,4} supplies an explicit stable-motif counterexample to variation contraction. This is not a mere restatement or table computation; it supplies a universal structural inequality and sharp asymptotic.
